parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) One difference between a longitudinal wave and a transverse wave is that a longitudinal wave consists of compressions and rarefactions.

ms.label: 5(a)(i)
ms.text:
(compression region:) particles / they close(r)
(rarefaction region:) particles / they far / further apart

ms.label: 5(a)(ii)
ms.text:
(longitudinal) oscillations / vibrations parallel to direction of wave (motion) / energy transfer OR medium is required OR cannot be
polarised
(transverse) oscillations / vibrations perpendicular to direction of wave (motion) / energy transfer OR medium not required OR can
be polarised

parts.label: i
parts.text: (b) (i) A sound wave of frequency 0.120 kHz travels through a rock at a speed of 3500 m / s. Calculate the wavelength of the wave. wavelength = ........................................................ [3]

ms.label: 5(b)(i)
ms.text:
v = fλ in any form OR (λ =) v / f
(λ =) 3500 / 120
(λ =) 29 m

ms.label: 5(b)(ii)
ms.text:
frequency not changed (in different medium)
audible / yes AND audible range 20 Hz – 20 kHz
